lines: Riley Chen
+1 (555) 010-7731 | riley.chen@example.com | example.com/in/riley-chen
EDUCATION
Northfield School of Management | MBA | Metro City, USA | Sep 2023 - Jun 2025
Lakeview University | B.A. in Economics | Lake City, USA | Sep 2014 - Jun 2018
EXPERIENCE
Coastal Marine Services | Diesel Mechanic | Lake City, USA | Jul 2025 - Present
- Rebuilt diesel engines and gearboxes for a fleet of 14 commercial fishing vessels, keeping dry-dock time under 5 days per job.
- Maintained hydraulic winch systems and logged service records for the harbor authority's annual inspections.
Crestline Logistics | Operations Analyst | Lake City, USA | Jul 2018 - Aug 2023
- Owned the weekly carrier scorecards for the regional managers and the monthly review meeting that discussed them.
- Cut warehouse pick errors 30% at two sites by redesigning slotting rules with the floor supervisors and retraining 45 pickers on the new layout.
- Ran the quarterly S&OP review across sales, finance and operations for 12 consecutive quarters, introducing a consensus forecast that cut forecast error from 18% to 11%.

- Led the rollout of a route-planning tool to 3 depots while rewriting the standard operating procedures, running driver training and taking over vendor negotiations for the telematics contract, which saved 1,800 driver hours a year across the region.
Harbor Payments | Associate Product Manager Intern | Metro City, USA | Jun 2024 - Aug 2024
- Redesigned merchant onboarding around a single verification step, cutting median time to first payment from 9 days to 4 across 2,300 new merchants in the pilot region.
- Lifted checkout conversion from 61% to 66% by testing a one-page flow against the three-step flow across 40,000 sessions, then shipping it to all merchants.
- Prioritized the dispute roadmap with RICE, scoring Reach as the number of support tickets each feature would close.
- After interviewing 25 merchants, mapping chargeback reasons, sizing the loss by segment and drafting a business case with finance, set the next quarter's roadmap priority.
- Ran the checkout A/B test with randomization by session and reported the 5-point conversion lift as the effect on merchants' customers.
- Presented the onboarding results and a follow-up roadmap to the payments leadership team, who funded the rollout to two more regions.
PROJECTS
Campus Food Rescue App | Product Lead | Student Venture | Oct 2023 - Present
- Launched a surplus-food pickup app to 3,100 students with two dining halls, redistributing 9 tonnes of food that would have been thrown away in its first year.
- Raised weekly active users from 400 to 1,150, a 150% increase, by adding pickup reminders chosen after 60 user interviews.
- Raised the pickup-slot fill rate by 20% across two dining halls, from 75% to 95%, by setting up a volunteer shift system.
MBA Consulting Practicum | Team Lead | Regional Hospital Network | Jan 2024 - May 2024
- Sized a $2.4M annual saving from consolidating outpatient scheduling across 4 clinics; the client funded a pilot based on the model.
- Patient intake at 4 clinics was mapped and the intake form was shortened, with the changes adopted by front-desk staff.
- Presented the final recommendation to the hospital COO and clinic directors, who approved a 90-day scheduling pilot at two clinics.
SKILLS
Product: roadmapping, A/B testing, user interviews, requirements writing
Tools: Jira, Amplitude, Excel

items.says: Put Harbor Payments before Crestline Logistics.
items.because: Recruiters expect reverse chronology, and the more recent product role deserves prominence.

items.says: Use consistent date formatting and punctuation, preferably en dashes.
Prevent awkward bullet breaks in the final PDF.
Keep the résumé to one page unless there is substantial additional relevant material.
Add a summary only if it efficiently explains the transition from operations to MBA and product work to diesel mechanics.
Tailor the skills and bullet emphasis to product roles.
items.because: Discovery, prioritization, experimentation, launch, adoption, and business impact should come forward.

items.says: Ensure the LinkedIn URL works and is customized.
Add a portfolio or project link only if it contains substantive product work.
Add city and state only if location matters for the target roles.
Confirm the phone number and email are professional and current.
Make the MBA completion status unmistakable.
items.because: Recruiters should not have to infer it from the dates.

items.says: Add a concentration, distinction, or leadership position only if it supports the target role.
Consider showing only graduation timing for the older degree if space is needed.
items.because: The older degree does not require as much detail.

items.says: Make the current diesel mechanic role support the product or operations narrative.
items.because: Coming after an MBA and product internship, it may confuse recruiters.

items.says: Give context for why a turnaround under five days is strong.
items.because: A prior average, service target, or avoided downtime would make the metric meaningful.

items.says: Clarify whether the rebuilds were completed personally, led, or done as part of a team.
items.because: The wording may overstate individual ownership if the jobs were collaborative.

items.says: Add repair reliability, repeat-failure rates, or economic impact if possible.
items.because: Turnaround alone does not show repair quality.

items.says: Show an accomplishment rather than routine maintenance responsibility.
items.because: The bullet currently reads as a responsibility.

items.says: Add scale or a result such as inspection outcomes, compliance, uptime, or defects prevented.
Reduce the emphasis on recordkeeping unless it improved inspection outcomes or compliance.
Replace or remove this bullet if there is no measurable result.
items.because: It is the first bullet the review would cut.

items.says: Replace responsibility language with decisions or improvements enabled by the scorecards.
items.because: The bullet says what was managed but not what changed.

items.says: Quantify the scorecards’ scope.
items.because: Carrier, region, manager, shipment-volume, or spend figures would establish scale.

items.says: Explain whether the scorecards improved service, cost, delivery, claims, or accountability.
Clarify the monthly review meeting’s outcome.
items.because: Saying it discussed the scorecards is vague and adds little.

items.says: Add the measurement period and baseline pick-error rate if available.
items.because: A relative reduction without a baseline is difficult to evaluate.

items.says: Clarify whether the error reduction was sustained after retraining.
Add the most relevant downstream impact if there was one.
items.because: Labor cost, rework, complaints, or order accuracy could show its value.

items.says: Define the forecast-error metric.
items.because: It is unclear whether it was MAPE, bias, or another measure.

items.says: Specify the business scope of the forecast.
items.because: Categories, revenue, facilities, or region would establish scale.

items.says: Remove the 12-quarter detail if space is tight.
items.because: Business scale matters more than the consistency it demonstrates.

items.says: Clarify whether you created or only facilitated the consensus-forecast process.
Focus the bullet on either operational rollout or vendor management.
items.because: It combines too many separate activities.

items.says: Clarify what produced the 1,800 saved driver hours.
items.because: The savings could come from route optimization, process changes, or both.

items.says: Add adoption, driver or route volume, cost savings, or service impact if available.
Split the bullet only if both parts produced distinct significant results and space permits.
Clarify whether all 2,300 merchants used the redesigned process.
items.because: They may instead represent the broader pilot population.

items.says: Identify your ownership in the onboarding work more precisely.
items.because: Discovery, requirements, coordination, experimentation, launch, and analysis are different contributions.

items.says: Address any fraud, compliance, or approval-quality tradeoff from one-step verification.
items.because: Stable guardrail metrics would strengthen the result.

items.says: Consolidate the checkout experiment with the later A/B-test bullet.
items.because: The same project appears twice.

items.says: Give the test period and say whether the conversion increase was statistically reliable.
State sessions as the direct measurement unit rather than implying unique customers.
items.because: Randomization occurred by session.

items.says: Clarify how repeat users appearing in both variants were handled analytically.
Support tickets each feature would close is not a sound RICE Reach measure.
items.because: Reach should be the affected population over a defined period; tickets closed sounds closer to impact.

items.says: Specify the time period used for Reach.
items.because: RICE scores are not meaningful without a defined time horizon.

items.says: Remove the RICE reference if the scoring was not methodologically sound.
items.because: Otherwise it may signal weak product-method knowledge.

items.says: Show what decision the prioritization changed.
items.because: Merely applying a framework is weaker than showing an outcome.

items.says: Give the sentence a clear subject and clarify your ownership.
items.because: It becomes grammatically indirect near the end.

items.says: Name the problem or feature area that became the priority.
Explain how interviews, chargeback analysis, and financial sizing affected the decision.
Consolidate this with the preceding roadmap bullet unless they describe different decisions.
items.because: The two bullets overlap.

items.says: Use the merchant interview count only if the sample represented the relevant segments reasonably well.
The checkout A/B test repeats the earlier conversion bullet.
items.because: The same project should appear only once.

items.says: Move its unique methodological detail into the stronger checkout bullet.
Align the causal claim with session-level randomization and measurement.
items.because: Session-level results do not necessarily establish an effect on all merchant customers.

items.says: Connect the funded expansion directly to the earlier onboarding work.
items.because: Recruiters should immediately see it as that initiative’s downstream result.

items.says: Clarify whether the two-region rollout happened or was only approved.
Use later rollout results if available.
items.because: The bullet currently stops at approval.

items.says: Make clear the food-rescue app was a genuine operating venture if it was one.
items.because: It should not look like a class exercise.

items.says: Define what the 3,100 students represent.
items.because: They could be registered users, eligible students, downloads, or active users.

items.says: Verify the nine-tonne figure and its measurement period.
Specify your product ownership in the launch.
items.because: Requirements, design, engineering coordination, and stakeholder management would show your contribution.

items.says: Avoid saying the food would have been thrown away unless diversion was measured directly.
items.because: Otherwise the claim may sound inferred.

items.says: The increase from 400 to 1,150 is 187.5%, not 150%.
Strengthen the basis for attributing user growth to reminders.
items.because: Interviews explain why the feature was chosen but do not prove it caused the growth.

items.says: Identify any experiment, phased rollout, cohort comparison, or pre/post measurement used.
items.because: It would clarify how the reminder effect was assessed.

items.says: State the period over which weekly active users increased.
The change from 75% to 95% is 20 percentage points, not a 20% increase.
items.because: The relative increase is 26.7%.

items.says: Explain how volunteer shifts improved pickup-slot fill rate.
items.because: The mechanism is not immediately obvious.

items.says: State the result’s period and whether it was sustained.
Use the plural “savings” rather than “saving.”
items.because: The singular is grammatically wrong here.

items.says: Distinguish projected savings from realized savings.
items.because: The current wording could be read as an achieved result even though it came from a model.

items.says: Add major assumptions or cost categories behind the estimate if useful.
items.because: They would establish the model’s credibility.

items.says: Replace passive voice with clear ownership.
Add a measurable result from the intake changes.
items.because: Form length, processing time, errors, or staff effort could show the effect.

items.says: Clarify whether adoption produced a demonstrated improvement.
items.because: Staff adoption alone does not establish one.

items.says: Distinguish your contribution as team lead from the team’s output.
items.because: The work may have been done collectively.

items.says: The pilot approval duplicates the approval in the first practicum bullet.
Consolidate the approval unless this bullet shows a distinct, relevant presentation skill.
Focus on what changed because of the presentation rather than who attended.
Clarify whether the pilot was completed and whether results are available.
List only skills supported by bullets elsewhere.
Ensure A/B testing reflects sound experimental practice.
items.because: The session-level measurement issue needs correcting.

items.says: Substantiate roadmapping with sound RICE scoring and an actual prioritization decision.
items.because: That would make the skill more credible.

items.says: Add other relevant product capabilities only if genuinely held.
items.because: Product analytics, prioritization, market research, stakeholder management, or KPI definition may be useful.

items.says: Indicate tool proficiency only when it is meaningful and defensible.
Add analytics or technical tools only if actually used.
items.because: SQL may be screened for, but should not be claimed without real competence.

items.says: Reflect meaningful Amplitude use in an experience or project bullet.
Show modeling, forecasting, or analysis in the experience to give Excel more value.
items.because: Excel alone is generic.
